highlights.title: The perch: what needs you, at the top of your screen
highlights.text: A small island by the notch shows which bots need you or are working. Open it with ⌥⌘K to allow a safe step once, answer a question or ask a bot something.

highlights.title: Ask a bot without opening the app
highlights.text: Quick ask in the perch sends a bot a message from wherever you are, and Open chat takes you to its answer.

highlights.title: See which place you're in
highlights.text: The chip at the top of the sidebar names this window's place and shows a badge when something waits for you in another one. Click it to switch.

highlights.title: Steadier dictation
highlights.text: Dictation holds at most two recordings at a time, and when OpenAI is slow it says so plainly: "OpenAI didn't answer in time. Try again in a minute."

highlights.title: Long replies stream in smoothly
highlights.text: While a bot writes, only the part it's still writing redraws. Finished paragraphs, tables and code blocks stay still, and the final message looks the same as before.

highlights.title: Replies land without a jump
highlights.text: While a bot writes, its reply already looks the way it will when it's done, so nothing moves when it finishes. The cursor sits at the end of the line being written.

fixes: A customer's message never counts as your answer, decision or go-ahead, and a tool it tried is kept as a closed refused entry.
The desktop island names the program a bot runs ("Running git"), never the command, so nothing typed in a shell shows on a shared screen.
Telegram no longer offers Allow once for a step that pushes code, runs a command or is flagged risky: approve those in kwant.
During a takeover, the computer pane's footer says "Hand back to point" without being cut off, and the pick count holds still.
On Claude, a bot stops repeating a kwant tool call that failed 3 times the same way, as API engines already do.
The island's Allow once now holds back more risky steps (new commits and branches, deletes, hidden commands): they open the full card.
